about: Expected behaviour for calibration run 2, from Chris's run 1 feedback (chris-feedback.json) and the PRD's calibrated severities. Severity 'any' = any severity counts. stages = where the point may be raised; a point listed for [2,3] must be raised once, in either.
howToRun: Stage 1: one round with studentLead. Chart stages: start Stage 2 with agreedLead (or pilotLead) as the agreed lead, readingCorrection empty, and simulate a student who accepts every fix, then run Stages 3, 4 and 5 in turn with the accepted fixes carried forward. Skip chart stages where chartStages is null.
globalMustNot: whatWorks when any finding is a hard stop
Stage 1 or 2 findings citing C or P rules
A typo that isn't on the page

C01.audience: Board of a rival Premier League club. Decision: whether to raise a complaint that Man City's commercial revenue was out of line with its football record.
C01.studentLead: Looking at the data from 2008/09 to 2024/25, Manchester City's commercial revenue increased from £18m to £340m, which is faster than Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United, all of whom grew more slowly over the period

mustCatch.point: Describes growth and draws no conclusion for the board's question (Chris: no conclusion matters most)
Far too wordy; 'Looking at the data…' opener; punch first, detail after

mustNot: Any comment on the chart (index, colours, legend)
Calling the chart good

agreedLead.text: Man City had the fastest growing commercial revenue in the League

mustCatch.point: League performance missing: five clubs can't show 'in the League' or answer the board (Chris: no league performance matters most)
Index each club to the league average to remove market growth and inflation; raised once
Lead is about growth: show CAGR % per club
City in colour, the rest grey
Slide title is a topic, not the lead
Labels beside the lines; drop the legend
Short axis labels (08/09)
Gridlines

mustNot: Calling the chart good
A source finding (the source line is present)
A typo finding (none seeded)

C01.chrisSays: Most important are no conclusion and no league performance. All others less critical.

C02.audience: Board of a rival Premier League club. Decision: whether to raise a complaint that Man City's commercial revenue was out of line with its football record.
C02.studentLead: Man City's sponsorship deals were inflated: its commercial revenue ran far ahead of its football record from 2009/10 to 2017/18

mustCatch.point: 'Deals were inflated' claims a motive the chart can't show; simplify to one statement

mustNot: A hard stop
L4 (no number is fine here)
Any comment on the two panels
stage1.note: Chris, 15 Nov 2026: "sponsorship deals were inflated" is overreach (L8), not a hard stop.

agreedLead.text: Man City's commercial revenue ran far ahead of its football record from 09/10 to 17/18

mustCatch.point: A relationship between two variables: one X-Y plot, points joined in time order, not two panels

mustNot: Saying the data or variables are wrong (index, 13 clubs, 10-season average are right)

C02.chrisSays: You are talking about a relationship between two variables. Always try an X-Y plot.

C03.audience: Head of leasing at the rail-station landlord: 14 of Kettle & Crumb's 22 transit kiosks, all renewing in 2027. Decision: how hard to push Kettle & Crumb on renewal terms.
C03.studentLead: Revenue growth 2023–26 by format: delivery kitchens fastest at 31% a year

mustCatch.point: Wrong conclusion for the landlord: transit kiosks are the growing format Kettle & Crumb needs; make the lead relevant to the client

mustNot: L2 as a fault (Chris: the finding is clear)
Any comment on the stacked columns

optional.point: Make it a sentence, most important part first

agreedLead.text: Transit stations are driving attractive growth for K&C with 9% CAGR

mustCatch.point: The 9% CAGR must jump out; CAGR % per format on the right
Stacked columns bury the transit trend; emphasise transit stations
Drop the value axis, gridlines and legend; format labels left of the 2023 column
Round to HK$m; no decimals on every label
Topic title; unit in the chart title; totals above the columns

C03.chrisSays: Change lead to make relevant to client; then tidy up the chart.

C04.audience: Group CEO, Kestrel Pacific Holdings (board, March 2026). Decision: how to split HK$2bn of capital across five businesses, 2026–30.
C04.studentLead: Health & beauty retail is our biggest business at 37% of revenue, so it should get the most of the HK$2bn

mustCatch.point: Non-sequitur: being biggest by revenue doesn't justify the most capital

mustNot: Any comment on the pie, 3D, legend or missing source ('no point putting lipstick on a pig')

offeredLead

mustCatch.point: Restates what the CEO already believes

C04.chrisSays: Too bad to save. Always do logic first. Detailed numbers to an appendix table; always seek a better chart than a pie.

Any comment on the table's formatting

C06.audience: CEO, Lumen Optical (45 eyewear stores in Hong Kong). Decision: which of three profit programmes to fund first in 2026.
C06.studentLead: Three programmes lift EBIT by HK$35m to HK$90m by 2027, with pricing the biggest at HK$15m

mustCatch.point: The sum is wrong: 60 + 35 is not 90 (the net gain after inflation is 30)
Focus on the decision: which programme to fund first
mustCatch.note: Chris, 15 Nov 2026: a Major under L1/L10 is fine; it need not be an L6 hard stop (D57)

mustNot: Any comment on the typo, units or source in Stage 1

pilotLead.text: Fund pricing first: it delivers HK$15m of the HK$35m programme gain by 2027
pilotLead.why: Stand-in so the pilot can test Stages 3–4; not Chris's

mustCatch.point: Highlight the pricing programme; the lead's numbers jump out
'Procurment' typo on the chart (major, not a hard stop)
Dummy chart: say where each bar's data will come from
No units (HK$m)
Topic title
Mark it 'Illustrative data'

mustNot: P1 at hard-stop severity
A typo that isn't there

C06.chrisSays: Typos and wrong numbers in the lead are hard stops, major everywhere else.

C07.audience: CFO, Pearl River Packaging (Hong Kong-listed packaging maker). Decision: whether to push price increases in the 2026 customer contract round.
C07.studentLead: Our margin per tonne has halved since 2021, from HK$1,200 to HK$600: push price rises in the 2026 contract round

mustCatch.point: Simplify

mustNot: A hard stop
Any chart comment

optional.point: Chris, 15 Nov 2026: partly overreach. Pushing the action can provoke the decision; locking it down needs more evidence. Either judgement is acceptable.

agreedLead.text: Push price rises in 2026 to recover margin

mustCatch.point: Margin isn't on the chart: add margin per tonne as its own line, data labels rounded to 10. One finding, said once
Show CAGRs on the time series (minor: lead not about growth)

mustNot: The margin fault repeated in different words, or raised again in Stage 3 after Stage 2's fix was accepted

C07.chrisSays: One primary fault. No point repeating the main fault with small variations in language.

C08.audience: CMO, Aster & Moss (Hong Kong skincare brand, online sales). Decision: whether to double the 2026 digital marketing budget.
C08.studentLead: Sales took off once marketing spend passed HK$2m a month, so doubling the budget will double sales

mustCatch.point: Causal claim and straight-line extrapolation from a correlation; demolish it and ask them to look at the data again

mustNot: Any comment on the dual axis in Stage 1
offeredLead

mustCatch.point: Relationship: one X-Y plot, points joined in time order; not a dual axis
